what_this_shows: What the City of Kitchener's published Active Transportation inventory contains, measured on one frozen snapshot: population, defaults, provenance, physical versus virtual records, and where it overlaps PathAble's Waterloo pilot.
what_this_does_not_show: That any Kitchener record describes the same thing as any OSM way or PathAble edge; proximity is descriptive and nothing is matched.
That any attribute is true on the ground; nothing has been field-checked.
That Kitchener evidence is independent of OpenStreetMap; the City permits its data in OSM and lineage has not been studied.
Any effect on routing; no Kitchener field is used by PathAble.

snapshot.publisher: The Corporation of the City of Kitchener

active_transportation.role: every published attribute; ACTIVE records only; no NETWORK LINKS category

walkability.role: pedestrian network including NETWORK LINKS; 12 fields; no STATUS

licence.name: Open Government Licence - The Corporation of the City of Kitchener

terms.attribution_text: the credit to use when crediting voluntarily
terms.personal_information_excluded: personal information is outside the licence

crs.transformation: Inverse of UTM zone 17N + NAD83 to WGS 84 (1) + axis order change (2D)
crs.proj_pipeline: proj=pipeline step inv proj=utm zone=17 ellps=GRS80 step proj=unitconvert xy_in=rad xy_out=deg

STATUS.basis: Lifecycle set by the City; new sidewalks enter as pending and become Active when houses are built (metadata: Maintenance).

FEATURE_TYPE.basis: Locations of bridges and other non-standard asset types; default SURFACE.

SURFACE_MATERIAL.basis: Type of surface material of the asset; default CONCRETE.

WIDTH_M.basis: Width of facility in metres from a coded list; documented 'default width 1.8m', schema default 1.5.

GRADE.basis: Maximum slope along the facility 'as calculated through a script'.

RAILING.basis: Presence of railing along the segment; default N.

CURBCUT.basis: Whether the facility is a curbcut down to street level; default N, U is unknown.

SURFACE_CONDITION.basis: Surface condition 'as found in the 2015 Trail inventory project'; default GOOD. Dated by the documentation, not per record.

LAST_INSPECTION_YEAR.basis: 'Last year feature was inspected through the sidewalker inspection program in Engineering or Operations trail inspections'. Records that an inspection happened, not what it found.

GRADE_CATEGORY_MAX.basis: Undocumented. Not attributed to any process by the City.

INSTALLATION_YEAR.basis: 'Year the asset was installed. Usually a database maintained field.'

width_zero_on_physical_record.rule: A physical facility cannot be 0 m wide; 0 is in the City's coded domain.

width_at_least_10m.rule: Wider than any pedestrian facility here.

last_inspection_year_not_a_plausible_yea.rule: Not a four-digit year up to the retrieval year.

slope_max_over_100_percent.rule: Steeper than 45 degrees along a walking or cycling facility.

date_after_retrieval.rule: A record date later than the snapshot.

condition_score_without_condition_date.rule: A calculated score without the date the City documents for it.

condition_date_without_condition_score.rule: A calculation date without the score.

roadsegment_side_out_of_domain.rule: A side value outside the City's LEFT/RIGHT/UNKNOWN/NA domain.

derived_slope_consistency.rule: GRADE_CATEGORY_MAX compared with the label its own text implies for SLOPE_GRADIENT_MAX (<2, 2-5, 5-10, >=10 percent); integer percents at a boundary are assigned to the higher band.

study_area.shape: axis-aligned rectangle (ADR 0006: a coverage extent, not a municipal boundary)

geography.label: Overlap feasibility only. A record intersecting the study area, or lying near a PathAble edge, is not a match.

evidence_on_pedestrian_records.scope: active physical pedestrian ways and crossings; a value counts only when it departs from the template default (a width of 0 is not counted)

geography.proximity_label: Distance from each intersecting record to the nearest PathAble edge, in the source's native metres. Descriptive; the transformation between the two datums is a null shift with a stated accuracy of a few metres, so the first bands are within that uncertainty.
geography.offset_label: Worst-point offset: every record line is sampled at least every 1 m and the largest distance from a sample point to the nearest OSM footway, path, pedestrian way or steps edge is reported (a directed Hausdorff distance). A small value means the whole line runs along OSM pedestrian geometry. It is consistent with shared lineage, and proves neither lineage nor a match.

sample.method: Records intersecting the study area, one stratum each by first matching rule; at least 3 per non-empty stratum, the rest of 80 by largest remainder in proportion to stratum size; within a stratum, ascending sha256(seed:snapshot_id:ACTIVETRANSPORTID).

unofficial_connection.rule: City's unofficial driveway and on-road connections

unresolved_semantics.rule: records whose physical or virtual nature the source leaves ambiguous

curb_cut_coded.rule: CURBCUT = Y (a curbcut down to street level)

not_along_osm_pedestrian_way.rule: pedestrian record with a point 20 m or more from any OSM footway, path, pedestrian way or steps

offset_from_osm_pedestrian_way.rule: pedestrian record whose worst point is 3-20 m from OSM pedestrian ways

merged_looking.rule: multi-part or at least 400 m long

split_looking.rule: shorter than 5 m without a curb-cut code

dense_core_sidewalk.rule: sidewalk in the densest tenth of the inventory in the study area

parallel_sidewalk_pair.rule: sidewalk whose road segment has sidewalks on both sides

residential_sidewalk.rule: sidewalk whose nearest OSM road is residential

other_physical.rule: cycling, maintenance and remaining physical records

adoption.routing_use: none — no Kitchener field is approved for routing by PA-GEO-03
adoption.decided_on: one snapshot, from the figures in each entry's basis

entries.subject: identity
entries.rationale: The City documents it as the permanent record id. It is present and unique on every record of both publications and joins them with no field disagreeing.

entries.subject: service row number
entries.rationale: The City documents that OBJECTID changes on export and import. The two publications happen to agree on it today, as the basis shows, but a value documented to change cannot identify a record across snapshots. It is used only to check that each request returned the rows it asked for.

entries.subject: source and source date
entries.scope: all values; SOURCE published by vocabulary class
entries.rationale: Record-level provenance: mostly the orthoimagery year a record was digitised from, with SOURCE_DATE matching that year. It dates the capture of the record, not any attribute on it.

entries.subject: record dates
entries.rationale: Database-maintained timestamps of record creation and of the last status change. Useful for lineage; not observations of the facility.

entries.subject: update date
entries.rationale: Nearly every record carries the same update day, written by the database account: it records a maintenance run, not an observation.

entries.subject: status
entries.rationale: Every published record is ACTIVE, which is also the template default, because only active records are published: the field distinguishes nothing in the open data. What the City asserts is the record's presence in its active inventory, which belongs to the record, not to this field. Planned, potential and closed records cannot be studied from the open data, and the network links carry no status at all.

entries.subject: classification
entries.rationale: Separates sidewalks, crossings, trails, links and connections, which is what a matcher needs to pair a record with the right kind of OSM way. It is not an accessibility fact.

entries.subject: stairs and structures
entries.scope: STAIRS, BRIDGE, OVERPASS, UNDERPASS, BOARDWALK only
entries.rationale: These are deliberate departures from the template value SURFACE and translate directly into steps, bridge and tunnel evidence. SURFACE is the template default and is never read as 'no stairs'.

entries.subject: geometry
entries.rationale: Centrelines digitised from orthoimagery. In the study area most pedestrian records run within 2 m of an OSM pedestrian way along their whole length, and the City permits its data in OSM. That does not establish independent geometry: until record-level history is inspected the geometry is treated as potentially shared-lineage — input to matching and a lineage question, not independent evidence of where a path is.

basis.crs_transformation: Inverse of UTM zone 17N + NAD83 to WGS 84 (1) + axis order change (2D)

entries.subject: width
entries.rationale: A value from a coded list, not a measurement. 1.5 is the template default and sits on almost every sidewalk; the documented 1.8 m default never occurs; 0 stands in for crossings and links. Other widths may be compared with OSM widths; none is adopted.

entries.subject: surface material
entries.rationale: Asphalt, stonedust, gravel, natural, brick, wood and the rest are deliberate departures from the template and translate into surface classes. CONCRETE is the template default and cannot be told from an unedited record.

entries.subject: surface condition
entries.scope: FAIR, POOR and UNUSABLE, as a claim dated 2015 by the City's documentation
entries.rationale: Documented as found in the 2015 trail inventory. A 2015 condition is not a current fact, so it may be kept only as a dated source claim. GOOD is the template default; UNKNOWN is explicit and most common, and stays unknown.

entries.subject: curb cut
entries.scope: Y only; N is never 'no curb cut', U is unknown
entries.rationale: Y marks short segments that are 'a curbcut down to street level' — a deliberate, located claim that translates into kerb-ramp evidence. Whether the ramp is lowered or flush is not stated. N is the template default.

entries.subject: railing
entries.rationale: Y is deliberate and N is the template default. PathAble's cost model has no railing input, so it can only be kept as a source claim.

entries.subject: grade
entries.rationale: Documented as script-calculated, and almost every record says UNKNOWN.

entries.subject: slope
entries.rationale: Derived by the City's FME script from an unstated surface model, with some values over 100%. PathAble derives grade from 1 m LiDAR itself; a derived value may be compared with it, never adopted over it.

entries.subject: grade category
entries.rationale: Undocumented, and it disagrees with the City's own SLOPE_GRADIENT_MAX on about half of the records where both are present.

entries.subject: condition score and date
entries.rationale: Documented as a calculated Cityworks score, but only 0 and 1 occur, and a score and its date almost never appear on the same record.

entries.subject: inspection year
entries.scope: plausible years, as the date a record was last inspected
entries.rationale: Documented as the last year the segment was inspected by the City's programmes. It says the facility was looked at, not what was found: it may date a record's existence, never an attribute.

entries.subject: installation year
entries.rationale: A single year covers a large share of populated values, which looks like a bulk load rather than installation dates; the documentation says only 'usually a database maintained field'.

entries.subject: virtual links
entries.rationale: The City's virtual street crossings say where its network connects. They are never a physical routable segment, and never evidence that a crossing facility exists.

entries.subject: unofficial connections
entries.rationale: Unofficial routes along roads or driveways, documented as such; not pedestrian infrastructure.

entries.subject: road relationship
entries.rationale: Which road and which side a sidewalk belongs to — what a matcher needs to pair it with OSM's sidewalk on that side. UNDEFINED is outside the City's own domain.

entries.subject: notes
entries.rationale: Documented as free text, but the snapshot holds only two workflow words whose meaning is not documented.

on_active_physical_pedestrian_records.scope: active physical pedestrian ways and crossings; a value counts only when it departs from the template default (a width of 0 is not counted)
